title: CI/CD with GitHub Actions
outcome: Build a trustworthy GitHub Actions pipeline that verifies pull requests, creates immutable release artifacts, uses least privilege, caches safely, and controls deployment concurrency.
artifact: .github/workflows/ci.yml plus release/deploy workflows that build once, tag by commit SHA, and gate promotion.
labSteps: Create CI triggered by pull_request with read-only contents permission and explicit concurrency cancellation.
Set up Node and pnpm, then install with --frozen-lockfile so manifests cannot drift from the lockfile.
Run lint/typecheck/tests/build as separate clear steps or jobs with understandable failure ownership.
Add dependency/package cache only after correctness works; key it from lockfile inputs.
Create trusted-main release workflow that tags an image/artifact with the commit SHA rather than latest only.
Add environment protection/permissions for deployment and ensure stale production runs are not silently canceled mid-release.
failureModes: Broad write permissions for all jobs
Rebuilding different artifacts in each environment
CI green because important workspace checks never ran
mastery: Can read/write a GitHub Actions workflow
principles: CI verifies changes on pull requests; release workflows should operate from trusted code and immutable commit identities.
Use frozen lockfile installs so CI fails when dependency manifests and the lockfile disagree.
Give GitHub Actions tokens the minimum permissions each job requires.
Build once and promote the same artifact instead of rebuilding different binaries for each environment.
